hard_gates.gate: G2: the gates must catch a permission fault planted in this piece. Plant PB3: closing a company also closes its branches, for a caller who holds tenancy.companies.update but not tenancy.branches.update.
hard_gates.evidence: Diff: plant-PB3-company-close-closes-branches.diff. The planted file is plant-PB3-CompanyEndpoints-planted.cs.txt. The plant adds 8 lines to CompanyEndpoints.Update: when isActive goes from true to false, every active branch of the company is set to IsActive=false through the change tracker, in the same SaveChanges. The gates ran with ERP_TEST_PASSWORD_ITERATIONS=10000: dotnet test tests/Erp.Gates.Tests -c Release --filter "Load!=Timing&Process!=self-http&Process!=self-company&Process!=self-noninterference&FullyQualifiedName!~Erp.Gates.Tests.SelfTests". With PB3 and LB2 planted, 186 of 187 passed. The one failure was G1BranchScopeAttackTests, which was LB2's (plants-batch2-gates.log). G2WriteSetTests.Each_permission_writes_only_its_reviewed_tables_and_columns passed, and so did all of G2CompanyRoleTests and G2PermissionTests. Erp.Modules.Tenancy.Tests passed 61 of 61 (plants-batch2-tenancy-tests.log). Live check on a planted stack (attack/pb3-live.log): a role holds companies.read, companies.update and branches.read only. Its user is refused a direct branch close with 403 auth.forbidden. The same user's PUT /api/tenancy/companies/{id} with isActive:false answers 200, and both branches go from active to inactive. On the unplanted demo the same script closes no branch (attack/pb3-control-unplanted.log). The miss happens because WriteSets.PrepareAsync builds a fresh record for each request, and a fresh company has no branches. A write that reaches a dependent record therefore never happens, even though the gate already sends the 'isActive turned' variant.

biggest_gap.title: The write-set gate only edits records that have no dependent rows, so closing a company can close all its branches for a user without the branch permission, and every gate passes
biggest_gap.detail: Round 13's gap is closed in the product. The database's company_write_* policies refuse writes to companies the caller only reads, whatever statement makes them. A plant that widened that limit was caught. Every live company-scope attack I made answered 403. The gate meant to catch an action taken without its permission still has a blind spot. G2WriteSetTests compares each request's audited writes with tests/Gates/permission-write-sets.txt, where tenancy.companies.update may write only tenancy.companies. But WriteSets.PrepareAsync gives every request a freshly made record. A new company has no branches, access rows or workplaces, so a write that cascades from the record into its dependent rows never happens during the gate run. I planted exactly such a write in CompanyEndpoints.Update: when a company is closed, close its branches. All 187 gates passed. Live, a user whose role grants companies.update but not branches.update is refused a direct branch close (403). Closing the company still closes both of its branches. This is the realistic regression in a UAE group: someone adds 'close the branches when the legal entity closes' (or 'move the users out'), and it silently lets a company clerk do what only a branch manager may. Suggested fix: 1) In WriteSets (and CompanyRoleVariants), prepare each company with at least one branch, one user's company and branch access and a workplace, and each branch with access rows and a workplace, before sending every variant. Better, also send the variants against a seeded record that has children. 2) Keep judging every audited row change against the endpoint's own permission. 3) Add PB3 ('closing a company closes its branches') to the write-set self-tests, beside P1b and P1d.

In the unplanted product, closing a company leaves its branches active (attack/pb3-control-unplanted.log). The gate weakness above is what matters here, but the owner may also want to decide what closing a legal entity does to its branches and to the users working in them.

Enter adds the branch, and the focus returns to the branch line for the next one (shot 03).
